newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco bans newspaper with no explanation.
newsitem.headline: Morocco bans newspaper with no explanation.

text.p: The government on Wednesday banned a weekly political newspaper, Morocco's most popular, a press union spokesman said.
The order to close Oussbou Assahafi Assiassi, which was signed by Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali, was effective from November 20, 1996, he said.

"The newspaper's editor Mustapha Alaoui was summoned on Tuesday to police headquarters and informed that the Oussbou Assahafi Assiassi was banned in Morocco but gave no explanation," the spokesman said.
Officials at the Communication and Interior ministries were not immediately available for comment.
In a statement sent to Reuters, the editor said the decision "violates the freedom of speech and the basic principles of human rights in Morocco."

The independent al-Oussbou Assahafi Assiassi has a circulation of more than 100,000 copies. In recent weeks it focused "critical and humourous articles on the centre-right government policy," a member of the union said.
In the late 1980's the interior ministry banned Al-Kawliss, another newspaper ran by Alaoui.
Morocco has a dozen daily newspapers and four weekly papers, half in Arabic and the remaining in French. Most reflect government views.
